LAYOUT SURVEY (from overview image-001.jpg)
- The packet has 36 images: 12 reduced overviews (image-001, -004, -007, ... -034), each followed by two native-resolution tiles (top half and bottom half of the same photograph).
- image-001 shows four separate small paper(?) leaves on black ground, arranged 2 x 2, with pencil shelfmark labels at the foot of each: "Stams, STA, Frg. 165/2-1r" (top left), "...165/2-2r" (top right), "...165/2-3r" (bottom left), "...165/2-4r" (bottom right). Small numbered tabs at top left of each leaf (1, 3, 5, 7). Colour checker bottom right.
- Each leaf: a single column of c. 17-18 long lines in a cursive gothic hand (bastarda/cursiva type), brown ink, no visible ruling. The lines are long and the leaf narrow, so each line carries only 3-5 words.
- Each leaf has rectangular black areas (holes or masking/cut-outs) at the left margin at regular intervals (about 4 per leaf); on 3r there are additionally grey rectangles at upper left (apparently image redaction or paper patches). These blacked areas interrupt the first word(s) of some lines.
- 1r: a large ornamental initial (looks like a cadel/strapwork initial, ink-drawn, not coloured) at about line 6-8 opening a new section; a short closing line (line 4, "...") before it.
- Leaves are foxed and stained; 1r is darker and more worn at upper part.
- Text appears continuous prose (Latin), no glosses or rubrics visible in colour; a few marginal stroke marks / "q"-like marks at lower left corners (possibly quire/catchmarks or just stamps).
- Tentative interpretation: leaves of a single small-format book cut into strips/leaves, possibly from a documentary or narrative prose text. Not more.
